title: Godot 4.6 beta 1 – Folder duplication bug when importing assets via drag & drop
body: ### Tested versions Dev snapshot: Godot 4.6 beta 1 mono ### System information Windows 11 Godot 4.6 beta1 mono RX7900XT Intel Core ultra 7 265K 32gb ram ddr5 ### Issue description Hello, I would like to report a possible bug encountered in Godot v4.6.beta1.mono While working on a project, I had a folder containing three simple sprite files (very lightweight assets). I imported the folder into Godot using the standard drag & drop workflow from the file system into the Godot editor. Unexpectedly, after the import, the folder was duplicated thousands of times inside the project. The total number of duplicated folders/assets grew to nearly 30,000 elements, which severely impacted the editor and forced me to manually remove them. This behavior seems unintended, especially considering the simplicity and small size of the original assets. I am attaching images to show the result after the import. Environment details: - Godot version: v4.6.beta1.mono - Platform: Windows - Import method: Drag & drop from OS file explorer into Godot editor - Assets: 3 sprite png images inside a single folder I wanted to report this in case it is a known issue or something that should be tracked for the beta. Thank you for your work on Godot and for taking the time to look into this. ### Steps to reproduce Steps to reproduce: Open Godot 4.6 beta 1. Create or open any project. In the FileSystem dock, create a new folder. Put a few lightweight assets inside the folder (in my case, 3 simple sprite images). Drag and drop that folder from the OS file explorer into the Godot FileSystem (or re-import it via drag and drop). After the import, the folder is duplicated many times automatically (in my case, it created thousands of duplicated folders, reaching nearly 30,000 items). Expected result: The folder should be imported once, containing the original assets. Actual result: The folder gets duplicated repeatedly without user action. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) The issue occurs in a completely new, empty project and does not depend on any project-specific settings or scripts. It only requires creating a folder with a few image files and dragging it into the Godot FileSystem, as described in the reproduction steps above.
